quests.instruction: Please don't talk ___ the lesson. Which word is missing?
quests.hint: The talking should not happen at any moment while the lesson is going on.
quests.explanation: 'During' shows that something happens throughout a period, or at some moment inside it. 'During the lesson' means while the lesson is going on.
quests.funFact: 'During' answers the question 'When?' with an event or a period, such as during the film or during the holidays.

quests.instruction: We saw lots of animals ___ our trip to the zoo. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We name the event in which we saw the animals.
quests.explanation: 'During our trip' means at some time while the trip was happening. 'Under' and 'across' do not show time.
quests.funFact: Zoos have helped to protect many animals that are in danger.

quests.instruction: It rained heavily ___ the night, but the morning was bright. Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: The rain fell at some point while it was dark.
quests.explanation: 'During the night' means at some time while the night lasted. 'By the night' would show a deadline, and 'on the night' needs a particular night.
quests.funFact: 'Overnight' also means during the night.

quests.instruction: Mia fell asleep ___ the film, so she missed the ending. Which word fits?
quests.hint: She missed the ending, so the film was still on.
quests.explanation: She fell asleep while the film was playing, so it happened during it. 'Before' would mean earlier than the film, and 'after' would mean the film was finished.
quests.funFact: 'Before', 'during' and 'after' show three different places on a timeline.

quests.instruction: Nobody may use a phone ___ the exam, but you can use it afterwards. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: The sentence says that afterwards is allowed.
quests.explanation: 'During the exam' means while the exam is going on. The sentence says phones are allowed 'afterwards', so the rule covers the time during it.
quests.funFact: Exam rules often say what you can and cannot do during the test.

quests.instruction: The shop is closed ___ the holidays, but it opens again in January. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The shop is closed for the whole holiday period.
quests.explanation: 'During the holidays' means throughout the holiday period. 'At' and 'under' do not fit a period of time like this.
quests.funFact: Many shops have shorter opening hours during the holidays.

quests.instruction: We have to wait ___ five o'clock for the shop to open. Which preposition fits?
quests.hint: We keep waiting up to that time, and then the waiting ends.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows that something continues up to a certain time. We wait up to five o'clock, and then it stops.
quests.funFact: 'Till' is a short form of 'until': wait till five.

quests.instruction: Grandma arrived on Monday and is staying with us ___ Friday, and then she goes home. Which word fits?
quests.hint: She stays for several days, up to Friday.
quests.explanation: 'Until Friday' means she stays up to Friday, and then stops. 'On Friday' would only name that one day.
quests.funFact: 'Until' and 'till' mean the same, but 'till' is more informal.

quests.instruction: Don't open the present ___ your birthday. It is a surprise! Which word fits?
quests.hint: You must wait all the way up to the day.
quests.explanation: 'Until your birthday' means keep waiting up to that day. 'By your birthday' would be a deadline, and 'at your birthday' does not fit.
quests.funFact: Surprise gifts are often wrapped so that nobody can see what is inside.

quests.instruction: Please hand in your homework ___ Friday at the latest. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: The homework must be finished no later than Friday.
quests.explanation: 'By' shows a deadline: no later than that time. 'Until' would mean something continues up to Friday.
quests.funFact: 'By' and 'until' are often confused, even by adults.

quests.instruction: The shop stays open ___ eight o'clock tonight, so there is plenty of time. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: The shop stays open all the way up to eight.
quests.explanation: 'Until eight' means it stays open up to that time and then closes. 'By eight' would be a deadline for something else.
quests.funFact: Use 'until' for something that continues, and 'by' for a deadline.

quests.instruction: Which sentence uses 'until' correctly?
quests.correctAnswer: I must stay at school until four o'clock.
options: I must stay at school until four o'clock.
I must stay at school by four o'clock.
I must stay at school during four o'clock.
quests.hint: Staying is something that continues for a while.
quests.explanation: 'Stay until four' means stay up to four o'clock. 'By four' would be a deadline for arriving, and 'during four o'clock' does not make sense.
quests.funFact: 'Stay' and 'wait' go naturally with 'until'.

quests.instruction: The library is open ___ nine to five every weekday. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We name the start of the opening hours.
quests.explanation: 'From … to …' shows the start and end of a period: from nine to five. 'At' is only for one moment.
quests.funFact: 'Nine to five' is also a phrase for an ordinary working day.

quests.instruction: We have no school from Monday ___ Friday next week because of the holiday. Which word completes the sentence?
quests.hint: After 'from Monday', we need the end of the period.
quests.explanation: 'From Monday to Friday' marks the start and the end. 'From … to …' go together.
quests.funFact: In American English, 'Monday through Friday' includes Friday.

quests.instruction: We can visit the museum ___ ten and four on weekdays. Which word fits?
quests.hint: Two times are named, and we can go at any time inside them.
quests.explanation: 'Between … and …' shows a range: any time from the first time to the second. 'At' needs one exact time.
quests.funFact: 'Between' always goes with 'and', not with 'to'.

quests.instruction: We waited ___ two hours at the airport. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: Two hours tells us how long, not when.
quests.explanation: 'For' plus a length of time tells how long something lasts: for two hours, for a week. 'During' goes with an event or period, not a length of time.
quests.funFact: 'For' answers 'How long?' and 'during' answers 'When?'.

quests.instruction: Ali practises the guitar ___ half an hour every evening. Which word fits?
quests.hint: Half an hour is the length of the practice.
quests.explanation: 'For half an hour' tells how long the practice lasts. 'During half an hour' is not used with a length of time.
quests.funFact: 'For' is also used for years: for three years.

quests.instruction: Which sentence tells us how long?
quests.correctAnswer: We stayed at the beach for three days.
options: We stayed at the beach for three days.
We stayed at the beach during three days.
We stayed at the beach in three days.
quests.hint: Three days tells us how long.
quests.explanation: 'For three days' tells the length of the stay. 'During' needs an event or period, and 'in three days' means after three days.
quests.funFact: We say 'for three days' but 'during the holidays'.

quests.instruction: I'll finish my homework ___ twenty minutes, and then we can play. Which word is missing?
quests.hint: She will finish after that amount of time has passed.
quests.explanation: 'In' plus an amount of time can mean after that much time has passed. 'For' tells how long an activity lasts.
quests.funFact: 'In twenty minutes' tells when it will be finished; 'for twenty minutes' tells how long you work.

quests.instruction: Tom read a book ___ an hour before bed. Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: An hour tells us how long he read.
quests.explanation: 'For an hour' tells how long he read. 'In an hour' would mean after one hour has passed.
quests.funFact: Reading before bed can help people to relax.

quests.instruction: The school will be closed ___ the holidays, which last two weeks. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The holidays are a period of time with a name.
quests.explanation: 'During the holidays' tells when the school is closed. The length, 'two weeks', would use 'for'.
quests.funFact: We say 'for two weeks' and 'during the holidays'.

quests.instruction: Mia's grandparents visit us ___ Christmas, when the whole family gathers. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The word goes with the whole holiday period, not one day.
quests.explanation: We say 'at Christmas' and 'at Easter' for the holiday period. For the single day we say 'on Christmas Day'.
quests.funFact: 'At Christmas' means around that time; 'on Christmas Day' means 25 December.

quests.instruction: It snowed ___ the morning of my birthday. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: The morning belongs to one particular day.
quests.explanation: When a part of the day belongs to a particular day, we use 'on': on the morning of my birthday, on Friday night.
quests.funFact: Compare 'in the morning' with 'on the morning of the race'.

quests.instruction: My cousin was born ___ the 21st century, just after the year 2000. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: A century is a very long period of time.
quests.explanation: We use 'in' for long periods: in the 21st century, in the 1990s, in 1955.
quests.funFact: A century is a hundred years.

quests.instruction: 'How long is the break?' 'It is ___ ten forty-five until eleven o'clock.' Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: The answer gives the start and the end of the break.
quests.explanation: 'From ten forty-five until eleven' gives the start and the end of the break. 'At' and 'on' only give one point.
quests.funFact: 'From … to …' and 'from … until …' can both describe a period.

quests.instruction: The baby slept ___ the whole afternoon, so Mum could rest. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The sentence tells how long the baby slept.
quests.explanation: 'For the whole afternoon' tells how long the sleep lasted. 'At' and 'on' do not give a length of time.
quests.funFact: We can also say 'throughout the afternoon' for the same idea.

quests.instruction: Which sentence about opening hours is correct?
quests.correctAnswer: The shop is open from nine to six, except on Sundays, when it closes at four.
options: The shop is open from nine until six, except in Sundays, when it closes on four.
The shop is open in nine to six, except at Sundays, when it closes in four.
The shop is open from nine to six, except on Sundays, when it closes at four.
quests.hint: Check the start and end times, the days and the closing time.
quests.explanation: 'From nine to six' gives the opening hours, 'on Sundays' uses 'on' for days, and 'at four' uses 'at' for a clock time. The other sentences mix them up.
quests.funFact: Shop signs often list opening hours with 'from … to …'.

quests.instruction: 'When can I see the doctor?' 'She is here ___ Tuesdays and Thursdays, from nine until noon.' Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: Tuesdays and Thursdays are days of the week.
quests.explanation: We use 'on' for days: on Tuesdays and Thursdays. 'From nine until noon' then gives the hours.
quests.funFact: A clinic often has different opening hours on different days.

quests.instruction: Which phone-call plan is written correctly?
quests.correctAnswer: I'll call you after lunch, at about two, on Friday.
options: I'll call you in lunch, on about two, at Friday.
I'll call you after lunch, at about two, on Friday.
I'll call you before lunch, in about two, in Friday.
quests.hint: Match each time word to the kind of time: meal, clock time and day.
quests.explanation: 'After lunch' shows order, 'at about two' uses 'at' for a clock time, and 'on Friday' uses 'on' for a day. The other sentences use the wrong small words.
quests.funFact: 'About' before a clock time means 'not exactly'.

quests.instruction: Sophie promises to be home ___ dark. She does not want to be outside at night. Which word fits?
quests.hint: She wants to arrive earlier than dark.
quests.explanation: 'Before dark' means earlier than dark. 'After dark' would be later, and 'until dark' would mean staying out up to that time.
quests.funFact: In winter, it gets dark earlier in the afternoon.
